claims.claim: Reviewers report that the campaign lacks split-screen co-op.

citations.review_text:
Loved being able to play a new HALO. Does it beat the original trilogy? No. But it comes back to the roots better than 4 and 5. I love the new equipment (like the grappleshot turning master chief into basically spider-man) and new weapons. An Open-world map means tons of room for exploring and customization. 

That said, I think it might be dying as there hasn't been a new battle pass released in a long time. There are parts of the map that aren't grapple-able, but they look identical to the places that are. I'd love to see all surfaces allow for grappling. I would also love for campaign customization. Being able to play the campaign with my own armor would be peak! Also, split-screen campaign. c'mon guys. It's been a staple of nearly every halo installment. Please add it! 

Overall, a solid game for the HALO franchise, but I would wait until a sale.

Honestly the gold standard for all first person shooters. Great to play with friends of any skill level. Campaign was abysmal and absolutely not worth even half their asking price, but the free multiplayer experience makes up for it. Kind of wild there's no local multiplayer but alas that is the way of modern gaming.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe encountering cheaters in multiplayer matches who use wallhacks or aim assistance.

citations.review_text:
Halo Infinite could have been a genuinely great multiplayer experience, but the hacking problem makes it an absolute joke.

There is nothing enjoyable about loading into a match, trying to have a legitimate gunfight, and getting completely destroyed by someone who apparently has the ability to see through walls, track your every movement, and land shots that should be physically impossible.

At some point, you stop questioning whether the enemy is actually good and start wondering which cheat program they decided to use today. It is ridiculous that legitimate players have to deal with this garbage while trying to enjoy a game they actually want to play.

Halo has always been about competitive multiplayer, memorable gunfights, and having a good time with friends. Instead, matches can feel like a competition between people actually playing the game and people who apparently need a computer to play it for them.

It is genuinely disappointing seeing a franchise like Halo end up in this state. I should be getting killed because someone outplayed me, not because they have the combined eyesight of a satellite and the aiming ability of a military targeting system.

Until the cheating situation is properly addressed, I have very little interest in wasting my time here. Absolutely pathetic.
not sure about campaign mode but I know that they don't have any control to prevent cheaters on top of that it honestly feel as though some of the plays are RNG based

single_points.text: One reviewer says all the menus take ages to load every time the game is started.

citation.review_text:
Really solid casual multiplayer, especially for a F2P title. 
I really enjoy Jeff Steitzer's high energy announcer delivery in this iteration. 

Depending on your region and desired playlists you may have difficulty finding matches. 
All the menus take ages to load every time the game is started, which can get a bit tiresome. Performance is acceptable, but I have found it somewhat unstable even on Windows systems.

single_points.text: One reviewer says that they missed a trigger in the campaign which would not let them activate the light bridge needed to progress.

citation.review_text:
The multiplayer is great one of my favorite Halo multiplayers. I heard it was bad at launch but they seem to have fixed it up pretty well and it runs pretty well too.

The campaign is also good I liked the story and the gameplay though it is a bit buggy sometimes. I was playing coop with a friend and we used the grappleshot to cut some corners (literally) but we must have missed a trigger or something because it would not let us activate the light bridge needed to progress. 

Another thing is on my system the campaign does not run very well at medium settings. I thought about lowering the settings to low but the game just does not look very good at low settings. 

Overall its a good multiplayer and a good campaign (albeit a bit buggy).
